goal: Get the intended Slack web workspace/account working on the receiving client through the existing peer transport, preserving the host session.
completionScope: Successful same-machine, two-profile extension transfer on Linux. Physical Mac/Linux and normal host-sign-in Case 1 remain open in Phase 7.
userDirection: Pause Outlook and work on Slack next.
authorization: User selected Real workspace, explicitly allowed the shared Slack session after the workspace-isolation warning, and approved optional extension permissions. Stop on logout/sign-in/MFA/device requirements. No IdP credentials, messages, reactions or workspace changes.
knownImplementationState: Exact Slack provider, strict session/source types, correlated peer protocol, request guards, consent/permission UI and ownership-aware cleanup implemented. The reviewed production build successfully transferred the real session through WebRTC.

observations.workspaceOnlyCredentialIsolation: unproven; broader shared-session scope explicitly authorized

localProbe.correctionEvidence: Exact Enterprise API origin matched source config and observed resources; one corrected isolated-client probe, not an auth-boundary retry

extensionSmoke.profiles: Two isolated Chromium profiles under tmpfs on the same Linux machine
extensionSmoke.firstRun: UI-initiated transfer reached succeeded; occupied-client repeat rejected with client_not_empty and preserved both sessions
extensionSmoke.reloadFinding: Chromium disabled a CDP-loaded unpacked extension on reload with unsupportedDeveloperExtension while Developer mode was off. Enabling Developer mode in the two temporary profiles restored normal unpacked reloads without repeating permission approval.
